newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Five killed in Pakistan sectarian attacks.
newsitem.headline: Five killed in Pakistan sectarian attacks.

text.p: Gunmen on motorcycles killed at least five people, four of them in a mosque, in apparent Moslem sectarian attacks in Pakistan's Lahore city, police said.

They said three men died instantly when six motorcyclists sprayed bullets in a Sunni mosque in central Lahore, capital of the central province of Punjab, during an evening prayer meeting. One from an unspecified number of injured died later.
The attack followed the killing of a Shi'ite sect activist, Jaffer Hussain, who was shot at his office in western Lahore by two gunmen riding a motorcycle, the police said.

There were no claims of responsibility. But the police said the shootings seemed to be the latest in a wave of attacks in Pakistan's most populous province for which rival militant groups of majority Sunnis and minority Shi'ites blame each other.
The Punjab provincial government said on Sunday it had decided to seize all literature fanning sectarian prejudices.

Sectarian violence is rife in Punjab, where militant Sunni and Shi'ite factions are engaged in a feud that officials say has killed more than 100 people so far this year, including religious scholars, lawyers and doctors.
Lawyers in Punjab boycotted courts on Saturday in a strike to protest against the killings of lawyers.

Sunni-Shi'ite disputes over Islamic beliefs have often spilled into violence in Pakistan, which cost at least 170 lives last year. Shi'ites form about 15 percent of Pakistan's population of more than 135 million, most of whom are Sunnis, but are the majority in neighbouring Iran.
